concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
question: Henry Vivian Derozio, a teacher at the Hindu College of Calcutta, promoted radical ideas and encouraged his pupils to question all authority. This movement became known as the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Young Bengal Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Henry Vivian Derozio**, a teacher at the **Hindu College of Calcutta**, was a prominent figure who introduced radical ideas among his students. He encouraged them to question authority and think critically.
 
• The group of Derozio’s students, influenced by his teachings, initiated the **Young Bengal Movement**, which sought to bring about a societal transformation based on liberal and rational principles.
 
• The **Young Bengal Movement** was characterized by its emphasis on freedom of thought, individual liberty, and opposition to outdated customs and superstitions in Indian society.
 
• The movement primarily consisted of young, educated Indians who were inspired by the ideas of the **European Enlightenment** and the French Revolution.
 
• Although the movement was short-lived, it laid the foundation for modern ideas of reform, rationalism, and questioning traditional norms in **19th-century Bengal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Henry Vivian Derozio:**

 
 
• Derozio, of mixed Indian and Portuguese descent, was a poet, teacher, and social reformer born in **1809**.
 
• He joined the **Hindu College of Calcutta** as a teacher at the young age of 17 and influenced students with his radical views on science, politics, and human rights.
 
• He was deeply influenced by the ideals of the **European Enlightenment**, which he imparted to his students.
 
 
 
• **Young Bengal Movement:**
 
 
• The movement emerged during the **1820s and 1830s** in Bengal under the inspiration of Derozio.
 
• Its participants, known as the "Derozians," included young intellectuals and students committed to questioning orthodox practices.
 
• The group sought reforms in areas such as caste discrimination, the position of women, and superstitious practices.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Movement:**
 
 
• Although the movement did not lead to immediate large-scale changes, it contributed to the rise of the modern reformist movement in Bengal.
 
• It inspired later reformers such as **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** and **Iswar Chandra Vidyasagar**, who worked on issues like women's education and abolition of sati.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Movements:**
 
 
• **Social Service League:** Founded by **N.M. Joshi**, focused on improving the living conditions of laborers and promoting workers' rights in the 20th century.
 
• **Justice Movement:** Aimed at securing rights for non-Brahmins in Tamil Nadu in the early 20th century, under leaders like **Dr. T.M. Nair** and **P. Tyagaraja Chetti**.
 
• **Servants of India Society:** Established by **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** in 1905, this organization focused on social reform and education rather than radical ideologies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Young Bengal Movement** can be considered one of the earliest instances of Western influence on Indian intellectual and social life.
 
• While it did not achieve direct political success, it helped to create a critical, reformist spirit among the educated youth of Bengal.
 
• The movement's emphasis on rationalism and individual liberty set the stage for the later socio-religious reform movements in India.
